title: Runtime Handshake Compatibility Prober for Shadow & Canary Traffic
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, low-latency compatibility 'handshake' prober that validates structured output and function-call compatibility before and during staged rollouts (shadow, canary, A/B). The prober must detect shape/schema diffs, argument-type mismatches, missing required fields, and semantic signature changes (e.g., a numeric field changing meaning) and feed a graded severity score into the rollout manager to trigger auto-unwind when thresholds are exceeded.

Scope and approach:
1) Preflight handshake: on model variant registration, run a deterministic schema extractor across the model's representative prompts and produce a canonical call-shape fingerprint (names, types, optionality). Store fingerprint in rollout metadata.
2) Runtime probe: for live shadow/canary traffic, run a fast comparator that checks (a) exact key set, (b) type/coercibility, (c) enum membership, and (d) presence of expected tool-call names. Generate per-invocation diff records with shallow diffs only (no deep object nesting inspection to keep latency low).
3) Semantic heuristics: augment shape checks with lightweight semantic validators — unit-scaling checks (e.g., seconds vs milliseconds), unit suffix patterns, and frequent-field value distributions. Flag probable semantic shifts separately from pure shape diffs to reduce false positives.
4) Dry-run sandbox: for high-severity diffs, run a sandboxed 'replay' of the invocation against a pinned golden model or shim to triangulate whether the diff causes execution differences downstream (e.g., missing param causing fallback). This step is sampled due to cost.
5) Scoring and hysteresis: compute a rolling severity score per rollout slice using weighted counts of diff types, sliding-window smoothing, and a probationary hysteresis period before auto-rollback to avoid noisy flips.
6) Integration: emit structured telemetry compatible with Console's rollout dashboard (per-route metrics, diff-rate, top offending fields, example invocations). Wire the score into automatic rollout policies (probation -> partial throttle -> full unwind).

Trade-offs considered:
- Latency vs coverage: we intentionally limit deep nested schema checks in the hot path to keep per-request overhead <1ms p50. Heavy checks run off-path or sampled.
- False positives: semantic heuristics and probation/hysteresis needed to avoid rollback storms for benign format changes.
- Cost: dry-run sandbox is sampled to limit GPU cycles.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prober attaches to canary and shadow routes and emits per-invocation diff records to the telemetry pipeline within 5s of request completion.
- Diff classifier achieves >80% precision on internal labeled dataset (we'll create a 4000-invocation test corpus of injected diffs).
- Auto-rollback triggers when the rollout slice severity score exceeds configured thresholds (configurable per-project).
- Rollout Console shows top-N offending fields and can open example invocations for triage.
- Unit and e2e tests for handshake extractor, runtime comparator, and scoring logic are present in the runtime repo.

Implementation notes:
- Handshake fingerprint: compact string (sha256 over canonicalized JSON schema) stored as rollout metadata.
- Comparator is implemented in C++ hot path with a thin Rust/Go shim for config and metrics to minimize runtime allocations.
- Telemetry: use existing event schema "invocation_diff.v1" and add fields: diff_type, diff_severity, offending_keys (top-level only), sandbox_result.
- Config surface: per-team thresholds, sampling rate for sandbox, probation window (seconds), and rollback policy mapping (severity -> action).

Open questions / risks:
- How to represent optional vs required fields across different model families (open models may be permissive)? Proposal: teams declare a "strictness" tier for each rollout.
- Ownership for golden/shim models for dry-run replay — Ops vs Evaluations team?
- Backpressure: if diff telemetry volume spikes, need adaptive sampling at ingestion.

Next steps:
- [ ] Prototype comparator with synthetic diffs and run against 3 internal models (chat, code, structured).
- [ ] Create labeled test corpus and evaluation harness (dataset + scorer).
- [ ] Ship telemetry schema and console widgets for the rollout view.
- [ ] Add automated rollback integration with rollout-manager and document playbook.

2025-02-22 - Design review with Product & Console: Console wants top-10 offending keys and ability to open raw invocation. Action: add example payload storage (TTL 7d).
2025-02-25 - Spike complete: built Go comparator prototype; median extra CPU 0.6ms on ibatch path at p50. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
2025-02-28 - Metrics review: synthetic test shows 12% of canary invocations produce low-severity diffs (mostly enum casing). Decided to add semantic-casing heuristic to reduce noise.
2025-03-03 - Engineering sync: landed telemetry schema and small Console mock. Next: integrate with rollout-manager and implement hysteresis scoring. Assigned follow-ups to Asha and infra team.
